query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a controlled thermo‐mechanical processing regime (comprising specific rolling and annealing steps) to a cast eutectic high-entropy alloy (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1) will produce an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with retained lamellar features that simultaneously improves both strength and ductility relative to the as-cast state.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a coarse or conventional eutectic microstructure lacking the refined duplex lamellar features.
generation.intervention: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing involving controlled deformation (such as rolling) followed by precise annealing to inherit and refine the composite lamellar microstructure into an ultrafine-grained duplex form.
generation.conditions: The intervention should be performed under processing conditions where temperature, strain, and annealing time are optimized to avoid overaging or grain coarsening; results are expected to hold for alloys similar in composition to AlCoCrFeNi2.1 prepared via casting.
generation.structural_mediator: Ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure with inherited lamellar (composite) features.
generation.mechanism: The refined duplex microstructure is expected to generate a two-hierarchical constraint effect that helps to distribute stresses, along with a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism, both of which contribute to enhanced strength while maintaining or improving ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Both yield strength and ductility (e.g., elongation to failure) will be significantly improved compared to the as-cast baseline. While the exact magnitude may vary, a concurrent enhancement in these mechanical properties is anticipated.
generation.baseline: The as-cast microstructure of the eutectic high-entropy alloy without additional processing.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is applicable under processing conditions optimized for maintaining the fine duplex lamellar structure; deviation from these parameters (e.g., excessive annealing leading to grain growth) may not yield the predicted improvements.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative improvement in strength and ductility depends on the processing parameter optimization and may vary with slight changes in processing conditions and alloy compositions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples of an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy. One set is processed via the standard as-cast route (baseline) while the second set undergoes the proposed tailored thermo-mechanical processing (controlled rolling followed by optimized annealing). Conduct tensile tests and microstructural analysis (using SEM/TEM) on both sample sets.
measurements: Microstructural characteristics (grain size, duplex lamellar distribution)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed samples do not show a statistically significant simultaneous increase in both strength (yield and/or ultimate tensile strength) and ductility (elongation) compared to the as-cast baseline, or if the refined duplex lamellar structure is not observed, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Enhanced strength–ductility synergy in ultrafine-grained eutectic high-entropy alloys by inheriting microstructural lamellae

Abstract: Realizing improved strength–ductility synergy in eutectic alloys acting as in situ composite materials remains a challenge in conventional eutectic systems, which is why eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), a newly-emerging multi-principal-element eutectic category, may offer wider in situ composite possibilities. Here, we use an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA to engineer an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that deliberately inherits its composite lamellar nature by tailored thermo-mechanical processing to achieve property combinations which are not accessible to previously-reported reinforcement methodologies. The as-prepared samples exhibit hierarchically-structural heterogeneity due to phase decomposition, and the improved mechanical response during deformation is attributed to both a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.
